title: The calendar is a control surface

status: evidence-backed draft; recording, named interviews and owner-final approval remain open
hook: New York Fashion Week begins before the first look: somebody has to allocate the clock.

longform.headline: The calendar is a control surface
longform.opening: New York Fashion Week begins before the first look: somebody has to allocate the clock. The evidence reveals a system of coordination rather than a single machine.

sections.heading: 1945: coordinated time
sections.copy: A CFDA history note dates Ruth Finley’s Fashion Calendar to 1945; its scarce resource was not a seat but coordinated industry time.

sections.heading: 2014: CFDA ownership
sections.copy: The CFDA says it acquired the Fashion Calendar in 2014, owns and organizes the official schedule, and uses a formal inclusion application.

sections.heading: 2026: seventy scheduled presentations
sections.copy: Beyond the announced September 2026 dates and preliminary lineup, no later official schedule architecture is treated here as settled.
